lead.label: 14p
lead.why: Abstract: 'Alkylchlorinated compounds 14p-r were active on both the promastigote and amastigote forms, with emphasis on compound 14p, which showed strong activity against the amastigote form (IC50 = 0.6 uM ...)'; also 'Compound 14p was active against all the strains tested'. (14g and 14o are also highlighted in the abstract; 14p is the one named first and for the strongest potency.)

reactions.source: Scheme 1(a), main text p.4; no experimental procedure given, ref. 28 cited
Scheme 1(b), main text p.4; called '5-nitrofuraldehyde chloro-oxime 17' in the text

reactions.conditions: Chloro-oxime 17 (2 mmol), acetylene (2.2 mmol), CuSO4.5H2O, sodium ascorbate, KHCO3, THF/CH2Cl2 1:1, r.t., 48 h; recrystallised from hot EtOH, 68%
reactions.source: General procedure 4.1.2 and entry 14p in Experimental; Table 1 (R1 = CH2Cl); main text p.3

notes: The two preparation steps for chloro-oxime 17 appear only as Scheme 1 (reagents, conditions, yields) with ref. 28; there is no experimental procedure for them in the article (no SI supplied). I treated Scheme 1 as explicit since conditions and yields are given; if the rule is read strictly (procedure text required) this is route_not_explicit. The intermediate oxime has no name or label in the paper (label 16 is mine; the intermediate is not drawn in the text layer, derived from 'NH2OH.HCl' and 'chloro-oxime'). The text calls the aldehyde '5-nitrofuraldehyde 15' without stating it is purchased; treated as commercial. The paper says alkyl/chloroalkyl acetylenes 22k-q are 'commercially available reagents'; 22p taken as propargyl chloride from Table 1 R1 = CH2Cl. Lead choice: the abstract also highlights 14g and 14o; 14p picked as the compound named with 'emphasis'. The nitrofuran is on C3 and R1 on C5 of the isoxazole, as in the SMILES (nitrile-oxide from the chloro-oxime adds to the terminal alkyne).
